record.paper_title: Long time behaviour of one facilitated kinetically constrained models: results and open problems
record.original_question: For the Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model in dimension d ≥ 2 at infection density q > 0, consider the finite-volume process on the box Λ_n^d with a choice of boundary condition or conditioning that makes the chain ergodic. Is the mixing time of this ergodic finite-volume chain always linear in n for every q > 0?

evidence.quote: Finally, a related question in higher dimensions is the scaling with n of the mixing time of the (ergodic) chain on Λdn. The conjecture is a linear scaling for all values of q > 0, but, once more, that has been proved only for q large enough [10].

However, due to the presence of constraints, the logarithmic Sobolev constant is either infinite for the process on the whole lattice, or very large (i.e. Θ(n)) for the chain on the finite set Λn = {0, 1, . . . , n} with either appropriate infected boundary conditions ensuring irreducibility or conditioned on having at least one infection.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $d\ge 2$ and a parameter $q\in(0,1)$. For $n\ge 1$, let $\Lambda_n^d=\{1,2,\dots,n\}^d$. The Fredrickson–Andersen one-spin facilitated (FA-1f) model on $\Lambda_n^d$ is the continuous-time Markov chain on configurations $\eta\in\{0,1\}^{\Lambda_n^d}$ (where $\eta_x=1$ is interpreted as "infected/empty" and $\eta_x=0$ as "healthy/occupied") with the following dynamics: at each site $x\in\Lambda_n^d$, independently at rate $1$, the value $\eta_x$ is resampled (set to $1$ with probability $q$ and to $0$ with probability $1-q$) provided that the kinetic constraint $c_x(\eta)=1$ holds, where $c_x(\eta)=1$ if and only if at least one neighbour of $x$ in $\Lambda_n^d$ (or in the boundary) is in state $1$; otherwise the update is suppressed.

To make the chain irreducible, impose a boundary condition or conditioning that ensures ergodicity (for example, infected boundary conditions on $\partial\Lambda_n^d$, or conditioning on the existence of at least one infected site). The unique invariant measure is then the corresponding (conditioned) product Bernoulli($q$) measure $\mu$. Define the mixing time
$$T_{\mathrm{mix}}(n,d,q)=\inf\Bigl\{t\ge 0:\max_{\eta}\bigl\|P_t(\eta,\cdot)-\mu\bigr\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le 1/4\Bigr\}.$$

Question: Is it true that for every $d\ge 2$ and every $q\in(0,1)$, one has $T_{\mathrm{mix}}(n,d,q)=\Theta(n)$ as $n\to\infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the mixing time of the ergodic finite-volume FA-1f chain on $\Lambda_n^d$ scales linearly in $n$ has been established only in the regime where $q$ is sufficiently close to $1$ (linear precutoff in finite volume with suitable boundary conditions). For general $q>0$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, the conjecture remains open as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Front evolution of the Fredrickson-Andersen one spin facilitated model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of FA-1f dynamics in finite volume and front evolution; full mixing-time linear scaling for all q in d>=2 not established.
status_evidence.claim: Linear mixing-time scaling proved only for q large enough; general case open.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Fredrickson-Andersen one spin facilitated model in stationarity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses spectral gap and relaxation properties of FA-1f in d>=2 with results restricted to specific regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Mixing time bounds in d>=2 are partial; full conjecture remains open.
